parsedVerdict.reasoning: PlaceOrderUseCase does what an application use case should: it coordinates the steps and leaves the business rules to the domain. execute() loads products through the domain-defined ProductRepository port and turns invalid input into domain objects using Quantity.create and OrderItem.create. It passes stock reservation to the domain method product.reserveStock, builds the aggregate with Order.create, and saves it through the OrderRepository port. The file has no persistence code, no transport or HTTP handling, and no framework logic. Its only rule of its own is a guard that throws an error when a product is not found, and that kind of check belongs in the application layer. The private generateOrderId() makes the order ID using Date.now() and Math.random(). It could arguably be moved behind an ID-generator port or into the domain, but creating identifiers inside a use case is generally accepted for the application layer. It is not a clear case of logic that belongs in another layer. I found no ADR text that says otherwise.
